title: Animal Freedom Library!
content:
We couldn’t be happier to announce this. The Talon Conspiracy was a website that archived hundreds of animal liberation and earth liberation magazines, providing a platform to look into the past, learn from what the movement did decades prior, and plot the next steps for total liberation.

For a while, Talon was not available. Now, a new website has been launched, allowing you to read all the content Talon had. Go and check it out, from single zines from the 80s and 90s to long running publications like HOWL or the ALFsg magazine, there are heaps and heaps of material to read and learn from, for free, available to download or read online!

Go visit the Animal Freedom Library right now, and share far and wide, everybody should know about this!

title: Animal Rights Radicals Destroy Several Hunting Hides in Italy amid Controversy over Hunting Law Reform
content:
Several hunting hides in Veneto have been wrecked and covered in anti-hunting graffiti. Images released by four hunting organisations show the Animal Liberation Front (ALF) signature and messages opposing the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation.

Vandalism against hunting facilities is making headlines in Italy once again. Several hunting hides (capanni da caccia) have been destroyed in the Veneto region, with their structures covered in graffiti opposing hunting and the reform of the legislation governing it in the country.

The incidents were publicly condemned this Wednesday, 4 November, by four organisations in the sector: the Cacciatori Veneti association, CONFAVI, ACR and FCR. The organisations released a gallery of photographs showing the damage to the facilities and the inscriptions left on their structures.

The graffiti includes the familiar ALF signature, standing for Animal Liberation Front (Animal Liberation Front), alongside messages calling for a boycott of the reform of Italy’s hunting law. The symbols visible in the images match those used in previous actions attributed to this animal rights movement.

The organisations accompanied the photographs with a strongly worded message directed at those responsible for the damage: “Destroying other people’s property does not defend any cause; it only demonstrates cowardice.”

title: Two Activists Face Terrorism Charges After Releasing Nearly 700 Minks From Fur Farm in Midnight Raid
content:
November 6, 2026 Matthew Russell GreaterGood.com

By the time police arrived, the suspects were gone. The Cooldown reports that prosecutors allege Cara Ashley Mitrano and Christopher Jacob Legere, both from Worcester, Massachusetts, entered a farm building, opened cages, and released 683 minks. They also allegedly took genetic record cards used for the farm’s breeding program.

This was not the Stahl farm’s first ordeal. Unicorn Riot reports that the farm had been targeted before, when between 6,000 and 8,000 minks were freed in a separate incident linked to the Animal Liberation Front. No one was charged for that earlier raid.

After the second incident, the Stahl family said security cameras — installed following the first break-in — made all the difference. 2822 News notes the upgraded system alerted the farm and police almost immediately.

Farm co-owner Mark Stahl reported losses of $164,000, according to The Cooldown. All but 58 animals were eventually recovered. title: Magpie Liberated, Trap Destroyed (UK)
content: All across the UK, magpies are used as live bait in Larsen cages to trap and kill other magpies. The conditions of these majestic wild birds are horrendous – forced into a tiny wire cage filled with often multiple rotting bodies of other birds, no room to even stretch their wings. We happened to come across one in the countryside and released the imprisoned magpie and destroyed the cage. In solidarity with Des, an imprisoned vegan anarchist on turtle island.

title: Latest Essay by Maksym Kryvosh (Plokhoi), Liberation Prisoner in Ukraine
content:
I was taken from my cell to a room to participate in a court hearing remotely, via video conference. The court was considering a petition from the prison guards to place me in solitary confinement for two months. (For the kleptocracy known as Ukraine, it wasn’t enough that I’ve been in solitary for seven years, or the 13-year sentence I was awarded for fighting for Justice; they also had to throw me into the punishment cell for periods ranging from 14 days to three months—bringing my total to 18 stints in the punishment cell over three years).

The judge was reading out the ruling, but I wasn’t listening anymore, nor was I looking at the monitor. I was looking at the window—a large moth was beating its wings against the glass. It was unclear how it had gotten there; the windows were sealed shut. I told the guards: I won’t go back to the cell until I set it free… It worked! Outside, I opened my palms; it was a Peacock butterfly—the most beautiful butterfly I had ever seen—its colors shimmering and mesmerizing in the sunlight. title: Lies the Fur Industry Tells!
content:
Mink and fox killers and their apologists often say the most ridiculous things to try and mitigate their losses after raids like the two we have seen in the last couple of months, in which 3000 or more captive mink were liberated from horrific captivity. Sample absurdities spouted as fact include:

Lie #1: Many or most of the escaped animals were run over and killed by cars.

– The absurdity of this statement is that before liberation, death was 100% certain. Every animal on the farm was bred to die by the end of November. While it is true a small number may be hit by cars after being released, most will not, and if nothing else they have been given a chance at freedom. In reality, fox and mink farms are located in rural areas with little traffic, the animals are quick and solitary animals, and it beggars belief to imagine them aggregating in the road waiting to be run over by the rare passing vehicle.

– Mink are in fact only a few generations removed from their wild cousins and have not yet had their wild instincts bred out. The “Mink Rehabilitation Project” led by convicted ALF liberator Rod Coronado proved this decades ago. title: 100 Hens Liberated from a Barn in France
content:
We believe that the structures of speciesism are vulnerable and accessible.

Last week, we – an anonymous group – went to a factory farm in France and helped 100 hens escape from it. A few hours later, the liberated hens were already running on the grass and petting each other.

Rage consumed us when we arrived at the barn. The sky was dark, and everything was silent except for their screams and talks inside.

We entered and took them out, as fast as we could. After that, the night didn’t have the same color. We could hear them talk in their transport cages but we knew that they were free from harm, at last.

And, of course, we still deeply think of the ones who are still inside. We will continue to fight so that, one day, everyone could be free and safe.

If you can, please go inside those places of oppression, open the cages and take them out. You will experience more rage, fear and hope that what you are probably used to but every second of it will be so worth it. Because when you go on with your daily life later, you will know that the people you helped escape are now free and safe.

Thank you to everyone who fight alongside other animals and good luck with your actions.

title: Activists Release 1,500 Mink From Idaho Farm
content:
Activists called the raid on an Idaho mink farm “liberation” for the 1,500 minks they released. But they can’t take care of themselves, said the farm’s owner, leaving many to die of heat, stress or get run over. “This is an unethical thing to do,” he said.

Intent on liberating caged animals, masked protesters broke into a family-owned mink farm in southeast Idaho, less than 80 miles west of Wyoming, and released 1,500 mink into the wild on Saturday.

Farm owner Jeff Hobbs told Cowboy State Daily that instead of freedom, the activists delivered a death sentence, leaving the animals to perish from dehydration, stress, heat or getting run over on the road.

“This is an unethical thing to do to animals,” Hobbs said. “Regardless of your value system, I haven’t quite figured out how you can claim that you’re doing something for the benefit of the animals that’s so harmful to them.”

When he spoke to Cowboy State Daily on Tuesday, Hobbs said he was still working to gather the loose minks in Franklin County. At this point, he said about 90% of the mink have been caught but still face health risks from the trauma of being temporarily released.

“This stressed them hard,” Hobbs said. “You stress animals and you run into problems. You have to do something to offset that stress so this has created a serious herd health problem.”

Hobbs said the break-in happened around 2:30 a.m. Saturday.
